janitorPolicy.title: Policy
janitorPolicy.caption: What this environment's janitor does. Fields marked Default follow Settings, General; change a field here to override it for this environment.

loadFailed.title: Couldn't load the janitor policy.
loadFailed.body: Check the connection and try again.

state.defaultTooltip: Set in Settings, General. Change it there to change every environment that follows it.

enabled.label: Janitor
enabled.switch: Run the janitor on this environment
enabled.helper: On by default. Turning it off stops scheduled runs; you can still choose Clean now.

keep.label: Exited task containers to keep
keep.helper: Per service slot, and per node for a global service. The newest few stay so you can still read why a task stopped. Default {{default}}.
keep.error: Use a whole number from 0 to 20.

grace.label: Grace period
grace.helper: How long something must have been stale before TierPlan removes it. The same period applies to containers, images and networks. Default {{default}}.
grace.error: Use a whole number of hours from 1 to 720.

networks.label: Also remove unused networks
networks.helper: Networks that no stack created and nothing uses. Off by default: without this they are only reported.

containers.label: Also remove stopped standalone containers
containers.helper: Containers started with docker run that someone stopped, once they are past the grace period. Off by default: without this they are only reported.

schedule.label: Schedule
schedule.helper: Server time ({{timezone}}). The exact start is spread out a little per environment so many environments don't run at once.
schedule.invalid: Enter a cron expression like 0 3 * * * (minute hour day month weekday).
schedule.tooFrequent: Runs can be at most once every 15 minutes.

conflict.message: {{user}} changed this policy while you were editing. Reload to see it.
conflict.messageAnon: This policy was changed while you were editing. Reload to see it.

sheet.title: What this policy would remove
sheet.description: Here is what the janitor would remove with the policy you've edited. Nothing is removed by saving.
sheet.appliesNext: Saving applies from the next run.
